role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: (fictional) A two-principal family office in Austin that owns four neighborhood strip centers and runs a small Python agent for lease math, protest deadlines and exchange timing.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Check Texas property-tax protest deadlines for four centers
Track 45/180-day 1031 deadlines and boot when a center sells
Price renewal and new-tenant proposals for 1,200-4,000 SF strip bays (net effective rent, percentage rent)
hardest_task: Sold a 38,000 SF San Antonio center for $4.2M (basis $1.35M, $1.9M loan, $210k selling costs) closing 2026-12-10; the agent must give the 45/180-day dates, check the identification list, and say how much debt or cash must be added to avoid mortgage boot when the Round Rock replacement is $3.9M with $1.8M new debt. It must also keep the four centers' protest filing dates straight.
data_it_needs: Deterministic dates and boot arithmetic; protest deadline with statute cite; NER for small-bay proposals; ideally Texas appraisal-district values and owner lookups (not on the hosted service).
dealbreakers: Any wrong deadline; output the owner cannot hand to the QI or tax adviser; needing a paid key for basic math.
budget_note: Would pay up to a few tens of dollars a month if it removed a missed-deadline risk; $49 is the ceiling.

role: ESG, energy benchmarking and building-performance compliance agent
deployer: (fictional) The sustainability office of a hotel REIT's New York portfolio (nine full-service hotels, 3,800 keys) running a Claude agent that prepares LL84/LL97 filings and capital-plan inputs.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
top_tasks: Estimate Local Law 97 emissions limits, excess emissions and penalties by property
Pull each hotel's LL84 benchmarking record (site EUI, GHG) for the filing
Put energy cost per occupied room and per key next to USALI metrics for the asset managers
hardest_task: For a 420-key Midtown hotel, compute 2030-2034 LL97 emissions limit versus actual (about 7,400 tCO2e) at $268/tCO2e, and show what energy-efficiency capex does to NOI at a 6.5% cap rate. The agent needs the verified limit coefficient for ESPM property type 'Hotel' and the filed LL84 numbers, both with citations.
data_it_needs: Verified LL97 limit tables by ESPM type and period, LL84 energy and GHG by BBL, building ID join (BBL to BIN), hotel NOI for the cap-rate step.
dealbreakers: A compliance number that is 'draft' or uncited; any tool that guesses an emissions coefficient; no way to tell verified from unverified.
budget_note: Would pay low hundreds a month only if the LL97 pack were verified and callable; the hosted free tier is a trial.

deployer: (fictional) The lease-administration group of a life-science landlord (2.1M RSF across Boston, San Diego, the Bay Area and Raleigh) running an in-house Python abstraction pipeline over scanned leases and amendments.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Abstract lease plus amendments into a current-state record with controlling clauses
Check tenant estoppels and rent rolls against the abstract before a refinancing
Catch hallucinated or misread terms before they reach Yardi
hardest_task: A 28,400 RSF lab lease from 2022 has a first amendment (2025) that extends the term three years, expands by 6,100 RSF and changes the pro rata share from 31.5% to 38.2%. The agent must produce the current abstract, flag what is unresolved (the new total area is computed, not quoted), and compare a tenant estoppel that still recites the old values. Across 140 leases this is where errors reach the lender.
data_it_needs: Quote-level verification with page and character offsets; amendment precedence; estoppel-vs-lease comparison; decommissioning, BSL and surrender clauses; privacy guarantees for confidential leases.
dealbreakers: Unflagged wrong values; lease text stored or logged; no way to show the quote to a reviewer.
budget_note: Would put a Pro or Team key in production if the hosted document tools are stable and the privacy commitments are contractual; would run the self-hosted build for the most confidential leases.

role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: (fictional) A solo net-lease investor in Indianapolis who owns eleven small single-tenant buildings (pharmacy, auto parts, dollar stores) and uses a private Custom GPT to screen listings and keep 1031 timelines.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Screen net-lease listings: implied cap rate, price per SF, remaining term
Size acquisition debt against DSCR and LTV with a rate shock
Track 45/180-day replacement-property deadlines for the next 1031
hardest_task: A 9,100 SF auto-parts building in a Midwest tertiary market is listed at $1.9M with $126,500 of year-1 NOI and a 10% bump in year 7. The agent must give implied cap and price per SF, max loan at 6.75% / 25-year / 65% LTV / 1.30x with a +100 bp stress, and an unlevered 10-year IRR at a 7.0% exit cap.
data_it_needs: Cap-rate and loan math with no hand-keying; tenant credit and comparable sales (not on the hosted service); a GPT that does not hallucinate numbers.
dealbreakers: A Custom GPT import that fails; any number the GPT computes in its head instead of calling the action.
budget_note: Pays for ChatGPT already; free tier is fine; would pay $49 only for credit and comp data.

role: Retail, restaurant and healthcare site selection agent
deployer: (fictional) A four-person real-estate team for a regional coffee and fried-chicken franchisee in metro Atlanta that scouts pad sites and in-line bays and negotiates the leases.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
top_tasks: Check a proposed drive-through coffee use against a center's exclusive and prohibited-use clauses
Compare a pad ground-lease proposal against an in-line bay on one occupancy-cost basis
Calculate percentage rent exposure for a store at forecast sales
hardest_task: The franchisee wants a 2,400 SF drive-through coffee pad at a 140,000 SF center whose anchor and an existing cafe hold exclusives; before offering $52/SF NNN with 10% bumps every five years and $60/SF TI, the agent must say whether any exclusive is in play and rank the pad against an in-line bay at $34/SF with $25/SF TI over 10 years at a 9% discount rate.
data_it_needs: Exclusive and prohibited-use abstracts with quotes; occupancy-cost comparison; traffic counts, demographics and parcel data (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: A conflict check that gives a false 'all clear' without saying so; numbers that cannot be replicated in the franchisee's Excel.
budget_note: Small franchise group; would pay a few tens of dollars only for something that stops one bad site commitment a year.

deployer: (fictional) A 35-broker tenant-representation boutique in Dallas whose brokers use a Claude copilot to build lease-proposal comparisons, renew-versus-relocate analyses and negotiation briefs for office, flex and mixed-use occupiers.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
incumbent_tools: the firm's own ARGUS-free NER template
top_tasks: Rank three or four landlord proposals on one occupancy-cost basis across NNN, base-year and expense-stop structures
Run renew-versus-relocate NPV with double rent, downtime and disruption
Turn landlord lease drafts into redline issues (exclusives, relocation rights, kick-outs)
hardest_task: A 120-person firm needs 18,000 RSF for seven years starting 2027-07-01: Las Colinas NNN at $24 with 4 months free and $40 TI, Uptown base-year gross at $33 with $0.75 bumps and $55 TI, Frisco expense-stop at $29.50 with $45 TI, with different load factors; and its current landlord offers a $30 renewal with a $180k allowance. The broker must hand the client one defensible ranking and the break-even rent that makes moving pay.
data_it_needs: A ranking replicable in Excel, with stated discounting, opex treatment and load-factor basis; market comps from the firm's own sources.
dealbreakers: Any ranking the broker cannot reproduce; hidden conventions; client data leaving without a clear statement.
budget_note: Firm budget for tools is modest per broker; a $49 key for the team would be an easy expense if the math reproduces.

role: ESG, energy benchmarking and building-performance compliance agent
deployer: (fictional) The sustainability analytics team at a mid-size office owner-manager (22 buildings, 5.5M SF in New York, Boston, Seattle and Denver) that scripts Claude Code to prepare benchmarking submissions and retrofit pass-through memos.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
top_tasks: Compute LL97, BERDO and Washington CBPS compliance positions per building
Model recovering energy-retrofit capex from tenants under green-lease clauses
Check each tenant's share of a retrofit and the savings cap
hardest_task: A 14-floor NYC office tower needs a $2.4M heat-pump retrofit to avoid LL97 penalties. The lease lets the landlord recover amortized capital items only up to demonstrated savings ($140k a year), over a 15-year useful life at 6%. The agent must show what is recoverable, what the landlord eats, and each tenant's annual share (42% and 30% tenants), citing the lease clauses.
data_it_needs: Verified LL97/BERDO/CBPS rules; capex recovery with savings cap and clause citations; energy data by building ID.
dealbreakers: Presenting a draft rule as verified; recovery math that hides the cap's effect; no citation to the lease clause.
budget_note: Would pay modestly for verified compliance packs; the free hosted capex math is a bonus.

deployer: (fictional) The acquisitions group of a $4B industrial investment manager based in DC that scripts Claude Code agents to pre-underwrite broker packages before the analyst opens ARGUS.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Quick DCF screen from an OM rent roll: value, NPV, unlevered IRR
Size acquisition debt on DSCR, LTV and debt yield
Run the LP/GP waterfall for the equity partner and see negative leverage
hardest_task: A 260,000 SF three-tenant industrial portfolio in the Baltimore-Washington corridor is offered at $36M (5.6% going-in cap). The agent must produce a 7-year unlevered DCF with 3% growth, 3% vacancy and 0.5% credit loss, a 6.25% exit cap and 7.5% discount rate; size the loan; then run an 8% pref / 12% hurdle / 20% promote waterfall on the levered equity, all in minutes so the analyst can decide whether to spend a day in ARGUS.
data_it_needs: DCF with documented conventions; loan sizing; waterfall; per-tenant rollover detail; market comps and rent growth assumptions (own sources).
dealbreakers: Undisclosed conventions that make results unreproducible; numbers that cannot be tied to an Excel check.
budget_note: Institutional budget is not the issue; a tool must replace a manual first pass. A paid key is easy to expense if the IRR ties to ARGUS-like logic.

deployer: (fictional) The hospitality valuation practice of a national appraisal and advisory firm (about 400 hotel assignments a year) that builds Copilot Studio agents inside its Microsoft 365 tenant to draft income approach sections.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Build a USALI-style stabilized operating statement and NOI for a hotel
Capitalize NOI with PIP and other deductions to an as-is value and per-key value
Check the cap-rate implied by a sale price before and after reserves
hardest_task: Appraise a 180-key select-service hotel: 75% occupancy, $150 ADR, NOI after a 4% FF&E reserve, an 8.75% overall cap rate, a $1.8M PIP deduction, and a $31.5M sale to reconcile; the report needs value per key, implied cap rates before and after the PIP, and the audit trail the reviewing appraiser can follow.
data_it_needs: USALI ladder with reserve, direct capitalization with deductions, value per key; STR comp-set data (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: Reserve double-counted or silently omitted; no per-key output; anything that cannot run in Copilot Studio.
budget_note: Firm-level subscription to a paid key is easy if the connector works in Copilot Studio; no appetite for an unverified connector.

deployer: (fictional) The asset-management team of a Mountain West hotel owner (11 select- and full-service hotels, $640M of debt) running a LangGraph agent that reads monthly operating reports and debt schedules and drafts the quarterly asset-management memo.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: a LangGraph agent with MCP adapters
top_tasks: Convert monthly P&Ls to USALI KPIs and flag occupancy, ADR and GOP margin variances
Rebuild each loan's amortization schedule, balloon and a yield-maintenance payoff for refinance decisions
Package the numbers with citations into the quarterly memo
hardest_task: For a $18.5M, 5.75%, 10-year loan with 24 months interest-only and 30-year amortization, actual/360, funded 2024-03-15, the agent must rebuild the schedule, tell the owner the balloon, and quote a yield-maintenance payoff at the end of month 32 (Treasury 4.25% plus a 50 bp spread, 1% floor) to evaluate a refinance, then roll that into the month's USALI KPIs.
data_it_needs: Reliable schemas for a framework (no $ref surprises), JSON errors the framework can parse, loan math with day-count conventions disclosed, monthly hotel KPIs.
dealbreakers: Tool schemas that break the framework's function-calling adapter; silent unit mistakes (monthly vs annual) that give plausible but wrong KPIs.
budget_note: A Pro key for the agent's batch runs across 11 hotels would be trivial; free tier covers a pilot.

deployer: (fictional) A mid-market retail landlord's lease-administration office in Chicago (31 grocery-anchored centers, about 4.2M SF) using Claude with custom connectors to run year-end CAM reconciliations and check lease clauses against what the tenants dispute.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Year-end CAM reconciliation for every tenant of a center with caps, gross-up, admin fees and base years
Percentage rent on grocery and pharmacy sales
Verify a CAM-cap clause a tenant is disputing against the lease
hardest_task: A 112,000 SF center: $1.011M of expenses of which a $210k roof replacement is not recoverable; 91% average occupancy grossed up to 95% on utilities; a grocer on a 4% compounding cap and a 10% admin fee that excludes parking-lot repairs, a pharmacy with a 15% admin fee, an inline tenant who moved out on 2026-08-31 with a year-over-year cap, and a base-year tenant.
